Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

Add a recency-weighted, popularity-adjusted directed-transition residual to per-dataset SASRec and train with multi-negative candidate-set cross-entropy. Use user-grouped cross-fitting for graph features during training to prevent a user's targets from directly entering their own graph statistics. The proposal explicitly targets incidental older-history influence, broad relatedness without a supported next-step association, and weak positive–negative separation, especially in Electronics.

 ## Search results
Evidence supports testing the objective before expanding history modeling, but does not establish the cause of weak Electronics separation. [Sampled-softmax analysis (2024)](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) connects normalized representations and temperature to discriminative gradients and reduced influence from extremely hard, potentially false negatives; its reported temperature range of 0.1–0.2 is a starting point, not a benchmark guarantee. [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) identifies sampled-BCE overconfidence and proposes generalized BCE. [eSASRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06450) also supports sampled softmax within a strong SASRec-style system, although architecture changes prevent attributing its gains solely to loss. [MINE+/InfoNCE+](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.08520) provides a decoupled contrastive alternative, with less direct evidence for this sequential benchmark.

Practical inference: retain the encoder initially; compare multi-negative BCE/gBCE, normalized sampled softmax, and a small decoupled-loss ablation under equal GPU budgets. Start with uniform negatives, then test a controlled random/semi-hard mixture; exclude known training positives and mask duplicate-target collisions. Hardness alone cannot distinguish difficult negatives from unobserved positives. [EMM (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0893608026004090) supports refreshed hard–random pools, while [ICLR 2025 research](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/2d2f85c0f93e69cf71f58eebaebb5e8d-Abstract-Conference.html) finds alignment can matter more than uniformity in sparse settings—so isotropy alone is insufficient. Diagnose embedding norms, mean cosine similarity, effective rank, and positive–negative margins using training data. Select exclusively by the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10; published gains do not establish transfer to its 99-negative evaluation.

---

Candidate-conditioned history attention has strong precedents. [TWIN-V2 (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.16357) retrieves target-relevant historical behaviors before applying target attention; clustering compresses very long histories. [VISTA (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.22049) instead summarizes history into cached tokens, then lets each candidate attend to those tokens. These support candidate-specific evidence aggregation, but their industrial CTR results do not establish gains on this Amazon next-item benchmark.

Complementarity requires more than semantic similarity. [SComGNN (AAAI 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02130) models both relevance and dissimilarity through low- and mid-frequency graph components. [Revisiting Graph Projections (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09209) offers a particularly relevant interaction-only baseline: directed weighted item graphs projected from user–item interactions. Directional association remains a behavioral proxy, however; ordered consumption alone does not prove functional complementarity.

No verified result found directly combines candidate-conditioned attention, directional complementarity, and sparse lexical features trained entirely from scratch. [MARS (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00702) motivates attribute-wise text matching but belongs to the pretrained-language-model setting. A constraint-compatible research hypothesis is separate history/candidate projections over item IDs plus TF–IDF or hashed title/description features, with recency-aware candidate attention and ordered-pair training. Separate projections permit asymmetric scores; lexical overlap alone does not. Compare against the cross-fitted transition baseline using matched validation candidates, with ablations for attention, text, and asymmetry. This is a proposed adaptation, not a published or measured improvement.

---

Recent work supports testing multiple intent representations, though it does not establish gains on this benchmark. ## Starting Research Idea
Add a recency-weighted, popularity-adjusted directed-transition residual to per-dataset SASRec and train with multi-negative candidate-set cross-entropy. Use user-grouped cross-fitting for graph features during training to prevent a user's targets from directly entering their own graph statistics. The proposal explicitly targets incidental older-history influence, broad relatedness without a supported next-step association, and weak positive–negative separation, especially in Electronics.
